newsitem.title: CANADA: NBA BASKETBALL-GRIZZLIES FIRE COACH WINTERS, NAME STU JACKSON FOR SEASON.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-GRIZZLIES FIRE COACH WINTERS, NAME STU JACKSON FOR SEASON.

text.p: The Vancouver Grizzlies, who have managed only 23 wins in their first two seasons, fired coach Brian Winters Friday and replaced him for the rest of the season with president and general manager Stu Jackson.
"I'd like to personally acknowledge the dedication that Brian Winters has made to this organisation," Jackson said at a news conference.

"Coaching an expansion team is a very difficult challenge and I'd like to thank Brian for his efforts and his contribution. However, I felt the team needed to go in a different direction. It is my judgment that a coaching change at this time was necessary."

Jackson returns to the coaching ranks after leaving the University of Wisconsin after the 1993-94 season to join the expansion Grizzlies. In two seasons with the Badgers, he guided the school to a 32-25 record and its first NCAA Tournament berth and post-season win in over 45 years.
Jackson rejoins the NBA ranks for the first time since being fired by the New York Knicks on December 3, 1990. In one season plus 15 games, he led the Knicks to a 52-45 record.

Jackson began his coaching career as an assistant at Oregon in 1981 and moved to Washington State from 1983-85. He became associate coach and head recruiting coordinator under Rick Pitino at Providence for two seasons before following Pitino to the Knicks.

After two years as an assistant in New York, he took over for Pitino in 1989 and posted a 45-37 mark that season. But the Knicks bowed out to the eventual NBA champion Detroit Pistons in the second round.

Winters was named Vancouver's first head coach in June 1995 after 10 years as an assistant with Milwaukee, Cleveland and Atlanta. The Grizzlies won their first two games last season, but came back to reality and finished with a 15-67 record.

This year's squad owns an NBA-worst 8-35 mark, and has shown little signs of improvement despite such promising youngsters as frontcourt players Shareef Abdur-Rahim, Roy Rogers and Bryant Reeves. The Grizzlies also established an NBA record earlier this month by becoming the fastest team to 100 losses.
Jackson's first game as coach will be Saturday when the Grizzlies host Denver.
